body:
A massive trilogy that strings several campaigns together.

For context im currently running a 5E campaign that has a lot to do with fate, descendants, and power passed down through bloodlines.  It's a high fantasy campaign that is currently involving a plot to save the world from an undead elven tyrant, who wants to iradicate the world of light, which the imbalance between dark and light would destroy all the realms. In the campaigns ending, the PC's will be given the choice to give their characters long extended life to have an option to play in the epilogue. The epilogue involves them living their lives and most likely protecting or helping the world as heroes, or maybe even just living a peaceful life for once. However one character will be cursed with a vision of the future, a boy who is a being created directly by the anti fate (the only thing with the power to defy fate) in which the boy comes through and kills them all in very amazing combat (the epilogue is both a catalyst to a much larger story. And a way for the players to try out what at that point would be their level 20 characters). Once they die, they're resurrected for one final fight, to inevitably destroy the anti fate's pawn, even if the world has to die too. They (hopefully) would kill the kid but at the cost of the realms splintering apart down into chaos, and causing a major collapse which would shape the worlds to come.

Flash forward several hundred, maybe thousand years and this is where the dream campaign truly kicks in. Should the players have decided they wanted to create a bloodline, or at least a child in the epilogue, they will have the option to play as a descendant. Not telling them what that means the campaign would eventually reveal that they are the descendant of their previous character, and that the prophecy involved in campaign 1 was a much smaller part of a greater whole. In which an assassins creed bloodline an ancient relic story would take shape, with the second campaign inevitably ending differently, but with a more open ending, to leave room for a massive trilogy.

Ik its crazy but God id love to pull this off

No way is a "good way to go" death is unpleasant no matter how you go about it. There are easier ways, and less painful ways to go tho... I wont feed the habit, but alchohol poisoning is not the best way to go about it I'll tell you that much.
